exposure: Mode of delivery (vaginal vs. planned pre-labor cesarean section)
cohort: Pregnant women recruited at prolonged pregnancy and planned pre-labor caesarean section clinics at University College London Hospital between February-July 2014 (n=171)
finding: Collecting maternal stool, baby stool, and cord blood samples from women around the time of delivery was feasible and acceptable for most women.
mod_finding: Women undergoing planned pre-labor cesarean section were more likely than those who delivered vaginally to provide ≥1 sample (98% vs 54%), but less likely to provide maternal stool (10% vs 43%).
